a: Several archaeological discoveries remain mysterious and continue to puzzle researchers. Göbekli Tepe in Turkey, dating to 9600 BCE, consists of massive stone pillars arranged in circles, carved with animal reliefs, built by hunter-gatherers before the invention of agriculture, completely upending the conventional timeline of civilization development. The Antikythera Mechanism, recovered from a shipwreck off Greece in 1901, is a complex bronze gear device from around 100 BCE that functioned as an analog computer to predict astronomical positions, a level of technological sophistication not seen again for over a thousand years. The Nazca Lines in Peru are enormous geoglyphs created between 500 BCE and 500 CE, depicting animals and geometric shapes, visible only from the air, their purpose still debated. The Voynich Manuscript is an illustrated codex from the early 15th century written in an unknown script that has resisted all decipherment attempts. The Moai statues of Easter Island (Rapa Nui) raise questions about how nearly 1,000 statues averaging 13 tons were transported and erected. Stonehenge in England required transporting massive bluestones 240 kilometers from Wales. The Indus Valley Civilization had advanced urban planning with sophisticated drainage systems, yet its writing remains undeciphered. The Baghdad Battery, a 2,000-year-old clay jar with a copper cylinder and iron rod, may have been an early electrochemical cell.
